synthesizedFacts.fact: Seborrheic dermatitis and rosacea are chronic inflammatory skin conditions that can coexist, with studies showing a significant overlap in patients.
Seborrheic dermatitis is often associated with Malassezia yeast, while rosacea may involve abnormal immune responses and neurovascular dysregulation.
Both conditions can cause similar symptoms such as redness, scaling, and itchiness, but rosacea is more likely to cause visible blood vessels and sensitivity.
Stress and environmental factors can trigger flare-ups in both seborrheic dermatitis and rosacea.
